correctness.rationale: For a weight-two translation, orbit pairs A_y and B_y yield same-color compatibility only at outside Hamming distance one and cross-color compatibility at distance ≤2. A clique can contain at most one edge from each color layer, and cross-distance bounds force all its outside vertices into one cubical square. A square block is C4*C4≈S3. Their mutual intersections lie in the thickened cube one-skeleton D_m, each square block attaching along a circle deforming onto that square boundary. Nullhomotopy of S1 into S3 gives, for each square, one independent S3 and a 2-cell filling the cubical boundary. Thus the total is Q_m^(2)∨F_m S3; Q_m^(2) is simply connected and homotopy equivalent to (V_m-E_m+F_m-1) S2, with m=n-2, and n=2,3 contractible. Independent orbit-pair enumeration and boundary ranks gave (β2,β3)=(0,1),(1,6),(7,24) for n=4,5,6. These finite instances corroborate, not prove, the unbounded decomposition.
